messages:
Emma - sales: Hey team — POC update from ACMEEdge: their TypeScript client hits a TLS handshake / proxy timeout when streaming responses through their corp edge. Happens reliably after ~15s of streaming, client shows `ECONNRESET` and server logs show aborted streams. They tried v1.3.2 SDK and also a raw curl test through their proxy and see the same drop.

Chris - solutions: Thanks — can you paste the client logs and the exact request they send? Also which proxy stack (corp fw / bluecoat / zscaler?)

Emma - sales: They said "forward-proxy with auth, corporate appliance" (no vendor provided yet). Logs from the TS SDK: 
```
2026-03-18T14:12:03.112Z INFO start stream request to https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream
2026-03-18T14:12:18.261Z WARN socket hangup after 15.1s
Error: socket hang up
    at connResetException (internal/errors.js:631:14)
    at TLSSocket.onConnectEnd (node:_tls_wrap:1429:16)
```
They also tried curl with `--http2` and got `curl: (28) Operation timed out after 15001 milliseconds`.

Ana - eng: Is the client setting a per-request timeout? TS SDK default deadline is 15s for initial response when behind certain proxies. If they're streaming long-running tokens we need to bump the handshake/idle timeout or enable keepalive on the proxy path.

Ravi - infra: On infra side, our streaming endpoints keep connections open. We see no aborts on our side for that connection id: `req-id=acme-98f7`. I suspect proxy idle timeout or intermediate proxy closing long-lived h2 streams.

Chris - solutions: Quick repro ask for customer: 1) try disabling HTTP/2 in the SDK to force h1 chunked streaming, 2) increase client socket timeout to 60s, 3) test using `curl --no-keepalive`. If that changes behavior we can confirm proxy closing h2 or idle TCP.

Emma - sales: They tested `curl --http1.1 --no-keepalive` and stream stayed open for 90s, no ECONNRESET. So seems HTTP/2 multiplexing + corp proxy = culprit.

Ana - eng: For TS SDK, workaround: set `preferHttp1: true` in the fetch layer or set env `REDWOOD_HTTP_VERSION=1`. Also bump `streamingTimeoutMs` to 60000 in their client config. Example: 
```js
const client = new RedwoodClient({
  apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY,
  preferHttp1: true,
  streamingTimeoutMs: 60000,
});
```
Note: preferHttp1 toggles the request to use chunked transfer with h1 which many corp proxies handle better.

Ravi - infra: We should also add server-side guidance and a troubleshooting KB. I'll add a temporary note in console docs explaining corp proxy behavior and recommend preferHttp1 for POCs behind managed proxies.

Chris - solutions: Can we provide a small test command they can run to verify fix (no SDK)?

Ana - eng: Yes — curl example to reproduce/verify: 
```
# force http1.1 + no keepalive
curl -v --http1.1 --no-keepalive -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?model=gpt-edge
```
If that stays alive and streams tokens it's a strong signal proxy h2 handling is flaky.

Emma - sales: ACMEEdge tried the SDK change and confirmed: streaming stable for 2+ minutes now. They asked if this will impact latency or throughput.

Ana - eng: Small tradeoff: HTTP/1.1 chunked can use more TCP connections under heavy concurrency; for single-connection POCs it's fine. For production, we can advise using Dedicated or Private with direct egress to avoid corp FW. Also offer quantized model variants if cost is a concern.

Chris - solutions: Next steps: 1) tell customer the workaround (preferHttp1 + increase timeout), 2) offer a short window of Dedicated trial to validate under their network, 3) follow up on security questionnaire item about outgoing TLS fingerprinting (they asked we don't use custom ciphers).

Emma - sales: I'll send the workaround and offer a 2-week Dedicated eval. Also sending a short note with step-by-step and curl sample. :thumbsup:

edge-agent-bot: Note created: presales/POC-ACMEEDGE-349999 — workaround documented in KB.

Ravi - infra: I'll add a short note for on-call: if we see repeated aborted streams with `x-forwarded-proto: https` + short duration, recommend asking customer to try preferHttp1 first.

Chris - solutions: Great. Closing the swarm for now. If ACMEEdge hits perf issues we'll reopen and assist with Dedicated routing. :eyes:
